_notice: Plain-English explanations of approaches. Members choose from this list and their profile prints the explanation, so nobody lists a modality without saying what it means. No efficacy claims.

records.name: Person-centred
records.desc: You lead. The therapist listens closely, does not direct, and works on the idea that you are the best judge of what you need to talk about.

records.name: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)
records.desc: Structured and practical. Looks at the link between what you think, how you feel and what you do, usually with tasks between sessions.

records.name: Psychodynamic
records.desc: Pays attention to patterns from earlier in your life and to what happens between you and the therapist. Often longer term.

records.name: Integrative
records.desc: Draws on more than one approach depending on the person and the moment, rather than following a single method.

records.name: Humanistic
records.desc: A family of approaches that focus on you as a whole person, your experience now, and your capacity to make your own choices.

records.name: EMDR
records.desc: Eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing. A structured approach often used with distressing memories, involving guided eye movements or other bilateral stimulation.

records.name: Couples and relationship therapy
records.desc: Sessions with both partners in the room, focused on how you communicate and what each of you needs.

records.name: Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT)
records.desc: Works on making room for difficult thoughts and feelings rather than fighting them, and on acting in line with what matters to you.

records.name: Coaching
records.desc: Goal-focused, forward-looking conversations. Coaching is not therapy and is not a regulated profession in the UK.
